title: Health & diet tracker with camera food capture, calorie logging, summaries, graphs, and in-app helper chat

requirements.text: Implement Internet Identity–based user flow so each signed-in user can create and view their own diet entries (no shared data across principals).

quotes: create an app about health it's about health and diet

acceptanceCriteria: Users can sign in/out with Internet Identity.
Creating diet entries while signed in associates entries with the caller principal.
A user cannot see another user’s entries when using a different principal.

requirements.text: Add a simple daily logging data model and persistence for food entries including: timestamp (day), food label/name, estimated calories, and basic nutrients (macros + a small set of micronutrients).

quotes: tell calories approx calories and basic nutritional values

acceptanceCriteria: Backend exposes CRUD methods needed by the UI to create and list entries.
Each entry stores calories and at least: protein, carbs, fat; and a small micronutrient set (e.g., fiber, sodium, sugar) as numeric fields.
Entries are persisted across page refresh and canister calls (stable storage).

requirements.text: Create a Daily Dashboard page that shows: today’s total calories, a list of today’s logged foods, and an end-of-day (and selectable date range) total calorie summary.

quotes: at last calories total calories summary

acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard shows today’s total calories computed from today’s entries.
Dashboard includes a date picker or range selector to compute totals for a selected period.
Users can add a new entry and see the totals update without a full page reload (React Query invalidation/refetch).

requirements.text: Add interactive graphs and rating-style visualizations for engagement, including: calories over time (daily), macro distribution (today or selected day), and a simple daily “nutrition balance” rating derived from logged macros.

quotes: so that it seems engaging not one-sided it should be interactive app

acceptanceCriteria: At least 2 graph types are present (e.g., line chart for calories over time; donut/bar for macros).
Graphs respond to user interaction (hover tooltips, day selection, or range selection).
A numeric/letter rating (e.g., A–F or 0–100) is shown with an explanation of how it is computed from macros, using clear English copy.

requirements.text: Implement a Camera Capture flow (preferring the device back camera when available) that lets users take a food photo and then create a log entry from it via an interactive estimation step.

quotes: user will scan the food through camera back camera

acceptanceCriteria: On supported devices, the capture UI requests the environment/back camera by default.
User can capture an image and preview it before saving/using it.
After capture, the UI proceeds to an estimation/confirmation step rather than auto-logging silently.

requirements.text: Provide an in-app “AI-like” chat helper experience for diet/nutrition confusion using an on-device/in-app rules + curated FAQ knowledge base (no external LLM calls), including suggested questions and citations to the app’s own guidance.

quotes: there should be an AI to chat also if user has any confusion

acceptanceCriteria: Chat UI supports back-and-forth messages with timestamps and clear assistant/user styling.
Assistant answers are generated from a deterministic curated knowledge base and/or rules stored in the app/canister (no third-party AI service calls).
Chat includes suggested prompts (e.g., “What is a calorie deficit?”, “How much protein should I aim for?”) and shows a fallback message when it cannot answer.

requirements.text: Add at least one clearly defined “unique” differentiator feature that is not just logging/graphs/chat: implement a “Confidence & Portion Adjuster” step when creating an entry (user adjusts portion size and confidence; calories/nutrients update live and the app stores the confidence value).

quotes: it should have unique features unique other than any app present currently

acceptanceCriteria: When creating an entry (including from camera capture), the user can adjust portion size (e.g., 0.5x–2.0x) and a confidence slider (e.g., Low/Medium/High).
Displayed calories/macros update immediately based on portion multiplier.
Saved entries persist both portion multiplier and confidence level and show them in the entry details.

requirements.text: Design a simple, easy UI with a coherent visual theme applied consistently across pages and components (colors, typography, spacing, and layout). Avoid a blue/purple default palette.

quotes: it should have a easy and simple user interface

acceptanceCriteria: UI uses a consistent theme (e.g., warm neutrals + green accents) across navigation, cards, buttons, and charts.
Primary flows (sign-in, dashboard, add entry, camera capture, chat) are reachable within 1–2 clicks from the main navigation.
All user-facing text is in English.

requirements.text: Add generated static image assets (logo + key illustrations) under frontend/public/assets/generated and render them in the UI (e.g., app header/logo and empty states).
acceptanceCriteria: Generated images exist in frontend/public/assets/generated with the exact filenames specified in imageRequirements.required.
At least the app header and one empty state use the generated images.
Images are loaded directly from static assets (not fetched from the backend).

constraints: Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or any paths listed as immutable (compose them instead).
Backend must remain a single Motoko actor (all logic in the main actor).
Do not integrate third-party LLM/AI services (no OpenAI/Anthropic/etc.); the chat helper must be implemented via curated content/rules within the app.
Do not rely on external databases or third-party food nutrition APIs; any estimation must use in-app/canister-owned data and user confirmation.
nonGoals: Exact calorie/nutrition recognition from images using a real ML model.
Medical diagnosis, treatment recommendations, or clinically validated nutrition planning.
Social features (followers, messaging, real-time chat) and push notifications.
